questions.subject: math
questions.question: Claim: the storm was severe. Which detail best supports it?
options: Three trees in the avenue were uprooted and a roof tile lay in the street.
questions.correct_answer: Three trees in the avenue were uprooted and a roof tile lay in the street.
questions.explanation: Uprooted trees are direct evidence of severity; a forecast is only a prediction.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Claim: the house had been empty for a long time. Which detail best supports it?
options: The house was built of stone.
The house has a red front door.
Dust lay thick on every windowsill and the gate hinges had rusted through.
The house is on a quiet road.
questions.correct_answer: Dust lay thick on every windowsill and the gate hinges had rusted through.
questions.explanation: Thick dust and rusted hinges take a long time to appear, which is exactly what the claim needs.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Claim: the road was steep. Which detail best supports it?
options: Cyclists dismounted and pushed their bikes for the last kilometre.
The road ran beside a field.
questions.correct_answer: Cyclists dismounted and pushed their bikes for the last kilometre.
questions.explanation: Pushing a bike uphill is a direct consequence of steepness.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Claim: the shop is popular. Which detail best supports it?
options: By noon on a Tuesday the queue stretched past two neighbouring doorways.
questions.correct_answer: By noon on a Tuesday the queue stretched past two neighbouring doorways.
questions.explanation: A long queue on an ordinary weekday is evidence of demand.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Claim: the team practised hard. Which detail best supports it?
options: They won most of their matches.
They were on the pitch before sunrise every morning for six weeks.
questions.correct_answer: They were on the pitch before sunrise every morning for six weeks.
questions.explanation: Winning shows results, not practice. Sunrise sessions over six weeks shows the practice itself.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Claim: the puppy was tired. Which detail best supports it?
options: It fell asleep in the middle of its own dinner bowl.
questions.correct_answer: It fell asleep in the middle of its own dinner bowl.
questions.explanation: Falling asleep mid-meal is a direct sign of exhaustion.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: She read the letter twice, then folded it without a word. What is implied?
questions.correct_answer: The letter troubled her.
questions.explanation: Reading twice and staying silent suggests the news was upsetting.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: The dog's bowl was full and the leash still hung on its hook. What is implied?
options: The dog had not been walked.
questions.correct_answer: The dog had not been walked.
questions.explanation: A full bowl and an unused leash imply the dog has not been taken out.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Maya's phone showed nine missed calls from the same number. What is implied?
options: Someone had been trying urgently to reach her.
questions.correct_answer: Someone had been trying urgently to reach her.
questions.explanation: Repeated calls from one number indicate urgency.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: The lights were off and the door was locked. What is implied?
options: The building was empty of furniture.
questions.correct_answer: No one was inside.
questions.explanation: Dark and locked together point to nobody being there; the other answers add details the text does not give.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: The kitchen smelled of bread and there were floury handprints on the table. What is implied?
questions.correct_answer: Someone had been baking.
questions.explanation: Bread smell plus flour is the trace of baking.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: He put on his coat and picked up the umbrella from the stand. What is implied?
options: He was about to go outside.
questions.correct_answer: He was about to go outside.
questions.explanation: The text shows preparation to leave. It does not state the weather outside.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Bees do not only make honey. As they move from flower to flower they carry pollen that lets many plants produce fruit. What is this mainly about?
options: The wider work bees do for plants
questions.correct_answer: The wider work bees do for plants
questions.explanation: The passage moves past honey to the pollen work, which is the point of 'not only'.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: The library closes at six, but the lights often stay on until eight. Every evening the same three volunteers can be seen at the back tables. What is this mainly about?
options: Volunteers keep the library open beyond its hours
questions.correct_answer: Volunteers keep the library open beyond its hours
questions.explanation: The closure time is six, so the detail that matters is who stays late and why.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: The river runs low in summer. Farmers along its banks take turns drawing water so that every field gets some. What is this mainly about?
questions.correct_answer: Farmers sharing scarce water
questions.explanation: The taking of turns is the central idea, and it exists because the water is scarce.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Learning a language takes many short sessions, not one long one. Ten minutes a day beats three hours on a Sunday. What is this mainly about?
options: Short regular practice works better than rare long practice
Ten minutes is enough to learn a language
Sunday is a good day to study
questions.correct_answer: Short regular practice works better than rare long practice
questions.explanation: Both sentences compare frequent short practice with infrequent long practice.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: The old bridge was closed for repairs, so the market traders took the longer road. Fewer customers came that week. What is this mainly about?
options: How a closed bridge reduced trade at the market
The best road to the market
questions.correct_answer: How a closed bridge reduced trade at the market
questions.explanation: The passage links a cause (the closed bridge) to an effect (fewer customers).

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Ravi checked the sky, then packed an umbrella, a coat and a torch before setting out. The road ahead climbed into the mountains. What is this mainly about?
options: Ravi preparing for a difficult journey
questions.correct_answer: Ravi preparing for a difficult journey
questions.explanation: Every detail is preparation for the climb ahead, not the trip itself.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Why might an author begin an article with a question?
options: To admit they do not know the answer.
To make the reader think about the problem.
questions.correct_answer: To make the reader think about the problem.
questions.explanation: An opening question draws the reader into the problem the article will address.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Why does an author mention their own childhood in an argument about schooling?
options: To give a personal reason for their position.
To prove the argument is correct.
To show they were a good student.
questions.correct_answer: To give a personal reason for their position.
questions.explanation: A personal anecdote supplies motive. An anecdote alone cannot prove a claim.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: A writer describes a house as 'tidy, quiet and cold'. What is the attitude?
questions.correct_answer: Disapproving
questions.explanation: 'Cold' turns the tidiness negative, which shows disapproval rather than admiration.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: Why does an advertisement repeat the price three times?
options: To show the price may change.
To make the low price the main point.
questions.correct_answer: To make the low price the main point.
questions.explanation: Repetition signals importance, and in an advertisement the repeated thing is the selling point.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: An article describes a factory worker's day in careful detail. What is the likely purpose?
options: To help readers understand the working conditions.
To explain how to get a factory job.
questions.correct_answer: To help readers understand the working conditions.
questions.explanation: Careful detail about a person's day is used to convey what the conditions are like.

questions.subject: math
questions.question: An author lists the dangers of a hiking trail in careful detail. Why?
options: To warn readers to prepare properly.
questions.correct_answer: To warn readers to prepare properly.
questions.explanation: A detailed list of hazards serves preparation rather than prohibition.
